name: Painted billboard sprites in a 3D diorama
worksWith: demo-kit painted cast and L-10 cutout heroes as art sources
oneLiner: Painted 2D characters stand in a three.js world as camera-facing billboards: yaw-only quads with their feet on the floor or tile top, the side they look at chosen on screen from the camera (target first, then move direction) with painted left / right variants and no mirror for art that must not be mirrored, walk frames advanced by distance (a hop for single pictures), attack / hurt / down motion, a hit flash inside the material, soft blob shadows, depth-correct alpha and screen anchors for 2D overlays.
fits: 3D tactics and grid battles with painted units
third-person or isometric 3D exploration with 2D characters
3D board and strategy games that want painted pieces
notFor: first-person games (sprites seen from above or very close look flat)
cameras that look straight down (pitch above about 60 deg)
games that need true 3D character animation, ragdolls or per-limb hit boxes
pixel-art 2D games without a three.js scene (use L-10 or a 2D sprite element)

needs: per unit, every frame: feet position x, z on the floor and the id it targets (or null)
floor height under a point: groundY(x, z) or the ground meshes
events: attack start, hit taken, death, restart / respawn
the art: kitSource (demo kit), or imageSource / canvasSource with the art's native facing and painted variants
provides: bb.add / move / setTarget / play / flash / set / update(dt)
bb.anchor(id, 'head' | 'feet' | 'center'): screen point in CSS px for bubbles, numbers, HP bars
bb.state(): per actor the drawn side read back from the quad uv, flipX, variant, target, screen x / y, facesMove
checks/facing-3d.py (8 directions x 4 camera yaws, 2 mutants), checks/feet.py (lowest opaque row within 1 px at 2x)

assets: none of its own: uses the demo kit (painted sprites with painted @left / @right variants) and the L-10 rigged heroes; any game art via imageSource / canvasSource
hostRequires: a three.js scene: three.js 0.149.0 as window.THREE (scene, camera, renderer)
